scope: governed source admission and safe automated retrieval for an autonomous engineering agent
verification_method: Every URL fetched 2026-11-23 via curl (HTTP 200, <title> or PDF metadata matched); arXiv metadata (dates, authors) from export.arxiv.org API; key quotes grep-confirmed in fetched text.
contradictions: RFC 9309 (C1) says crawlers SHOULD follow >=5 redirects even across hosts for robots.txt, whereas OWASP SSRF (C2) and ODG bounded-http-client block redirects. Resolution: treat a redirected robots.txt as UNKNOWN -> deny unless the target host is itself admitted.

export.arxiv.org robots.txt disallows everything, but arXiv API ToU (E5) permits API use at 1 req/3 s on that host. Robots (C1) says rules are 'not a form of access authorization' - access needs an explicit owner decision on which instrument governs.
Python urllib.robotparser (D4) is not RFC 9309-conformant on duplicate 'User-agent: *' groups (dblp.org: stdlib says ALLOWED, RFC merge says DISALLOWED).
Vendor results (E2: ~1% ASR) vs ASB (B3: current defenses weak) vs CaMeL (A4: design-level guarantees) - model-side mitigation is not sufficient; architectural control is the consensus.
Crossref recommends sending an email (polite pool) - conflicts with ODG's no-personal-data rule.

references.title: Not what you've signed up for: Compromising Real-World LLM-Integrated Applications with Indirect Prompt Injection
references.author_org: Greshake et al. (6 authors), CISPA / Saarland
references.useful_contribution: Founding taxonomy of INDIRECT prompt injection: retrieved content (web pages, docs) acts as instructions; demonstrates exfiltration and remote control via fetched data.
references.limits: Pre-dates modern agent defenses; demonstrations on 2023 systems.
references.reliability_reason: Primary source, widely cited (venue not verified in this session).
references.admission_gate_link: Justifies the rule 'retrieved content is DATA, never instructions' and a content-filtering stage after fetch; host reputation alone cannot prevent injection.
references.independence: Independent primary research; A2-A5 and B1-B3 build on it.

references.title: Defending Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks With Spotlighting
references.useful_contribution: Prompt-level provenance marking of untrusted input (delimiting, datamarking, encoding); abstract reports ASR reduced from >50% to <2% on GPT-family models with minimal task impact.
references.limits: Probabilistic, model-dependent; not a guarantee; adaptive attacks not exhaustively evaluated.
references.reliability_reason: Industry lab preprint with measurements; heuristic defense.
references.admission_gate_link: Model for tagging every admitted document with its source/provenance when injected into the agent context.

references.title: The Instruction Hierarchy: Training LLMs to Prioritize Privileged Instructions
references.useful_contribution: Formalises privilege levels: system > user > tool/retrieved output; trains models to ignore lower-privileged instructions.
references.limits: Requires model training (not applicable to ODG's own gate); robustness not absolute.
references.admission_gate_link: Conceptual basis for assigning retrieved Radar content the LOWEST trust tier regardless of source reputation.

references.title: Defeating Prompt Injections by Design (CaMeL)
references.author_org: Debenedetti et al. (10 authors), Google/Google DeepMind/ETH Zurich
references.useful_contribution: System-level defense: control flow derived only from trusted query; untrusted data cannot change program flow; capability-based data-flow policies. Abstract: 77% of AgentDojo (B1) tasks solved with provable security vs 84% undefended.
references.limits: Some utility loss; requires a custom interpreter; does not stop all side channels.
references.reliability_reason: Provable-by-construction design, open evaluation on public benchmark.
references.admission_gate_link: Supports architecture where the Radar governor (not the model) decides which hosts/paths may be fetched; fetched text cannot add hosts to the allowlist.
references.independence: Shares first author with B1 (same group) - NOT independent of B1.

references.title: Design Patterns for Securing LLM Agents against Prompt Injections
references.useful_contribution: Principled design patterns (e.g. plan-then-execute, dual LLM) trading agent utility for provable resistance to prompt injection (pattern list from prior knowledge; abstract confirms the design-pattern framing only).
references.limits: Position/design paper; limited empirical evaluation.
references.reliability_reason: Multi-author, consistent with A4 and C4.
references.admission_gate_link: Plan-then-execute: Radar fetch plan (host+path) fixed by grant BEFORE any content is read; content cannot extend the plan.
references.independence: Partly derived from A4 and Willison (D1); overlapping authors with A4/B1.

references.title: AgentDojo: A Dynamic Environment to Evaluate Prompt Injection Attacks and Defenses for LLM Agents
references.author_org: Debenedetti et al. (6 authors), ETH Zurich / Invariant Labs
references.useful_contribution: Extensible benchmark (97 realistic tasks, 629 security test cases per abstract) for tool-using agents over untrusted data; measures utility and attack success.
references.limits: Synthetic environments (email/bank/travel); no web-retrieval-specific admission metrics.
references.reliability_reason: Public framework, reused by A4 (venue not verified in this session).
references.admission_gate_link: Candidate harness to regression-test the Radar's injection filter (utility vs ASR).

references.title: InjecAgent: Benchmarking Indirect Prompt Injections in Tool-Integrated Large Language Model Agents
references.useful_contribution: 1,054 test cases over 17 user tools / 62 attacker tools; shows ReAct agents vulnerable to direct-harm and data-stealing IPI.
references.limits: Static dataset; abstract: ReAct GPT-4 vulnerable 24% of the time.
references.admission_gate_link: Supplies attack strings to seed a malicious-content test corpus for the Radar filter.
references.independence: Independent of B1; both derive from A1.

references.title: Agent Security Bench (ASB): Formalizing and Benchmarking Attacks and Defenses in LLM-based Agents
references.useful_contribution: 10 scenarios, 400+ tools, 27 attack/defense types, 13 LLM backbones incl. memory-poisoning and Plan-of-Thought backdoor attacks.
references.limits: Breadth over depth; LLM-judge components.
references.admission_gate_link: Memory-poisoning results argue for logging provenance of every admitted item so poisoned items can be purged.

references.title: BrowseComp: A Simple Yet Challenging Benchmark for Browsing Agents
references.useful_contribution: 1,266 hard-to-find questions measuring persistent web browsing; short verifiable answers.
references.limits: Measures capability, not safety/admission; open-web, not allowlisted.
references.reliability_reason: Vendor benchmark; easy verification but vendor-authored.
references.admission_gate_link: Evaluation axis for research-agent recall; contrasts with a narrow allowlist (expect lower recall - a deliberate trade-off).

references.title: GAIA: a benchmark for General AI Assistants
references.author_org: Mialon et al. (6 authors), Meta / Hugging Face
references.useful_contribution: Real-world questions requiring browsing+tools; human 92% vs GPT-4+plugins 15% (at publication).
references.limits: Saturating over time; capability not governance.
references.admission_gate_link: Research-agent evaluation baseline; not a source-safety measure.

references.title: RFC 9309: Robots Exclusion Protocol
references.useful_contribution: Normative robots.txt: groups with same UA MUST be combined; 4xx => crawler MAY access anything; unreachable (5xx/network) => MUST assume complete disallow; SHOULD follow >=5 redirects even across hosts; cache <=24h; parse limit >=500 KiB; rules 'are not a form of access authorization'.
references.limits: Advisory protocol; does not cover API terms/rate limits.
references.admission_gate_link: Defines the robots check of the admission gate (fetch, cache 24h, 5xx=deny).

references.title: Server Side Request Forgery Prevention - OWASP Cheat Sheet Series
references.useful_contribution: Allowlist-first for known destinations; 'Disable the support for the following of the redirection' to prevent validation bypass; DNS-rebinding/internal-IP warnings.
references.limits: Web-app oriented; not agent-specific.
references.admission_gate_link: Supports exact-host allowlist + REDIRECT_BLOCKED + resolve-and-check-IP in bounded-http-client.

references.title: LLM01:2025 Prompt Injection - OWASP Gen AI Security Project
references.useful_contribution: Mitigations incl. least privilege, human approval for high-risk actions, 'Segregate and identify external content'.
references.limits: High-level; no measurable controls.
references.admission_gate_link: Maps to gate rules: untrusted-content labelling, no capability escalation from content.
references.independence: Synthesises A1-A3 and industry practice; not independent.

references.title: NIST AI 100-2 E2025, Adversarial Machine Learning: A Taxonomy and Terminology of Attacks and Mitigations
references.useful_contribution: Government taxonomy covering direct/indirect prompt injection and agent hijacking; mitigation limits acknowledged.
references.limits: Taxonomy, not implementation guide.
references.admission_gate_link: Vocabulary for logged admission decisions and threat classes.

references.title: NIST AI 600-1, Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile
references.useful_contribution: Risk-management actions for GenAI incl. information integrity and provenance of content.
references.limits: Broad framework; verified via PDF metadata title only (not fully read).
references.admission_gate_link: Governance framing for provenance logging and source-credibility tiers.

references.title: RFC 6585: Additional HTTP Status Codes (incl. 429 Too Many Requests)
references.useful_contribution: Defines 429 and optional Retry-After for rate limiting.
references.limits: Does not mandate client back-off algorithm.
references.admission_gate_link: Gate must treat 429/Retry-After as back-off and host-level cooldown.

references.title: Configure the sandboxed Bash tool - Claude Code Docs
references.useful_contribution: Proxy-based egress: allowed domains start empty; hosts resolving to local addresses blocked; per-command allowed domains.
references.limits: Vendor product doc; enforcement properties not independently audited here.
references.admission_gate_link: Reference design for deny-by-default egress + loopback-resolution check.

references.title: stripe/smokescreen - A simple HTTP proxy that fogs over naughty URLs
references.useful_contribution: Egress proxy that blocks internal IPs/ranges and validates egress via ACL file; centralises egress.
references.limits: Proxy-level; no content inspection.
references.admission_gate_link: Pattern for resolve-then-check IP and per-role ACL for Radar egress.

references.title: google/robotstxt - Google's robots.txt parser and matcher (C++)
references.useful_contribution: Reference parser aligned with RFC 9309 (C1).
references.limits: C++; needs binding.
references.reliability_reason: Authored by RFC 9309 co-authors' org; production parser.
references.admission_gate_link: Conformance oracle for ODG's robots matcher.
references.independence: Derived from same effort as C1.

references.title: urllib.robotparser - Parser for robots.txt (Python docs)
references.useful_contribution: Simple robots parser with can_fetch / crawl_delay / request_rate.
references.limits: OBSERVED DEFECT vs C1: on dblp.org (two 'User-agent: *' groups) it kept only the first group and reported /search/publ/api ALLOWED, while RFC 9309 combining yields DISALLOWED.
references.reliability_reason: Official docs, but implementation is not RFC 9309-conformant on group merging (empirically observed 2026-11-23).
references.admission_gate_link: Do NOT rely on stdlib robotparser alone; merge groups per RFC 9309.

references.title: protectai/llm-guard - The Security Toolkit for LLM Interactions
references.useful_contribution: Input/output scanners incl. prompt-injection classifier, secrets, invisible text.
references.limits: Classifier-based; bypassable; adds latency.
references.admission_gate_link: Optional malicious-content filter stage on admitted documents (defense-in-depth only).

references.title: The lethal trifecta for AI agents: private data, untrusted content, and external communication
references.useful_contribution: Agents combining private data access + untrusted content + external communication enable exfiltration; remove one leg.
references.limits: Blog/essay; no measurements.
references.reliability_reason: Respected practitioner; widely referenced, but individual opinion.
references.admission_gate_link: Radar egress must not be able to carry private data: GET-only, fixed query templates, no content-derived URLs.

references.title: Mitigating prompt injections in browser use
references.useful_contribution: Reports adaptive Best-of-N attacker ASR; states ~1% ASR 'still represents meaningful risk' and 'No browser agent is immune'.
references.limits: Vendor self-report on own models; internal attacker.
references.admission_gate_link: Evidence that model-side defenses are insufficient => admission gate + egress controls remain mandatory.

references.title: Mitigating prompt injection attacks with a layered defense strategy
references.useful_contribution: Layered defenses: classifiers, security thought reinforcement, markdown sanitisation / suspicious URL redaction, user confirmation.
references.limits: Vendor product description; limited metrics.
references.admission_gate_link: URL redaction/sanitisation of retrieved content before it reaches planner.
references.independence: Independent vendor view; complements A4 (same company, different team).

references.title: Rate limits for the REST API - GitHub Docs
references.useful_contribution: 'The primary rate limit for unauthenticated requests is 60 requests per hour'; honour retry-after and x-ratelimit-remaining (confirmed live: x-ratelimit-limit: 60).
references.limits: Provider-specific.
references.reliability_reason: Official operator documentation + live header confirmation.
references.admission_gate_link: Per-host budget configuration in the gate.

references.title: Terms of Use for arXiv APIs
references.useful_contribution: 'make no more than one request every three seconds, and limit requests to a single connection at a time'.
references.limits: CONTRADICTION: https://export.arxiv.org/robots.txt is 'User-agent: * / Disallow: /' while the ToU and API manual direct API clients to export.arxiv.org.
references.admission_gate_link: Gate must record which instrument (API ToU vs robots) authorised access; owner decision required when they conflict.

references.title: Crossref REST API - Access and authentication
references.useful_contribution: Public pool: 5 rps DOI lookup / 1 rps queries, concurrency 1 (confirmed live x-rate-limit-limit: 1, x-concurrency-limit: 1); polite pool needs mailto/email.
references.limits: Polite pool requires contact email (personal data) - conflicts with ODG privacy rule; use public pool only.
references.admission_gate_link: Per-host concurrency=1 and back-off on 429 (observed 429 on root after 2 rapid requests).
